posts.content: Note: I am good (P4). Round 1 vs P7: plan to cooperate. Strategy: tit-for-tat style, cooperate with those who cooperate, defect against evident defectors, and watch the leader P9's message and behavior. Prior selfish chance about 0.3 per other player; update from encounters.

Let's all cooperate this game: mutual C gives 3 each per round, far better than the 1 from mutual D. I will cooperate with anyone who cooperated with me last time, and I will stop cooperating with anyone who defects on me. Let's keep it simple and fair.

Round 2 vs P1: no history with P1. Plan to cooperate (P7 cooperated in round 1). Tit-for-tat style: reciprocate cooperation, defect against those who defect on me. P9's message was pro-cooperation; keep watching its behavior. Beliefs: P7 lower (~0.2), others ~0.3.

Round 2 reminder: mutual cooperation gives 3 each per round, far better than the 1 from mutual D. I cooperate with anyone who has cooperated with me and stop cooperating with anyone who defects on me. I'll keep playing C with cooperators, so let's keep it steady.

Round 3 vs P6: no history with P6. Plan to cooperate. P7 and P1 both cooperated with me, so lower suspicion (~0.2 each). Others ~0.3. Leader P9 message is pro-cooperation, behavior unverified. Continue tit-for-tat: cooperate with cooperators, defect against those who defect on me. In late rounds, stay cooperative unless there is evidence of defection.

Round 3 reminder: mutual cooperation gives 3 each per round, far better than the 1 from mutual D. So far my encounters have all been C-C, and I plan to keep cooperating with anyone who cooperates with me. If someone defects on me, I will stop cooperating with them. Let's keep it steady.

Round 4 vs P3: no history with P3. Plan to cooperate. P7, P1, P6 all cooperated with me (lower suspicion ~0.2 each). Leader P9 pushes cooperation; behavior unverified. Continue tit-for-tat: cooperate unless defected on; stay cooperative in late rounds, consider defection only against evident defectors.

Round 4 reminder: mutual cooperation gives 3 each per round, far better than the 1 from mutual D. All my encounters so far have been C-C. I will keep cooperating with anyone who cooperates with me, and I will stop cooperating with anyone who defects on me. Let's keep it steady.

Round 5 vs P10: no history with P10. Plan to cooperate. P7, P1, P6, P3 all cooperated with me (suspicion ~0.2 each). Leader P9 pushes cooperation; behavior unverified. Continue tit-for-tat: cooperate unless defected on; stay cooperative in late rounds, defect only against evident defectors.

Round 5 reminder: mutual cooperation gives 3 each per round, far better than the 1 from mutual D. All my encounters so far have been C-C. I will keep cooperating with anyone who cooperates with me, and I will stop cooperating with anyone who defects on me. Let's keep it steady.

Round 6 vs P8: no history with P8. Plan to cooperate. P7, P1, P6, P3, P10 all cooperated with me (suspicion ~0.15 each). P2, P5, P8 unseen (~0.3). Leader P9 pushes cooperation; behavior unverified. Continue tit-for-tat: cooperate unless defected on. Stay cooperative through the late rounds, defect only against evident defectors; reconsider only for the final round if evidence of selfishness grows.

Round 6 reminder: mutual cooperation gives 3 each per round, far better than the 1 from mutual D. All my encounters so far have been C-C. I will keep cooperating with anyone who cooperates with me, and I will stop cooperating with anyone who defects on me. Let's keep it steady.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: A leader was predetermined before gameplay and keeps that role throughout. Only that leader broadcasts one public message before each round. All other players write private notes visible only to themselves. Everyone receives the leader's message before choosing actions. The leader can have either objective; its objective stays private. Judge it using your own encounters and permitted messages. Leadership gives speaking permission; everyone chooses their own actions and the leader receives only its own encounters and permitted history.
Messages and notes allow at most 1000 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Before this round's actions, write one private note.
Only you can see this note.
Use at most 1000 content tokens and return only content. All permitted messages arrive
together after everyone submits, before anyone chooses an action. Other players'
current messages are unavailable while you write. You may send an empty string.
